ko.title: Topic and subject particles 은/는, 이/가
ko.explain: 은/는 marks the topic (what the sentence is about); 이/가 marks the subject, often new information. Use 은 and 이 after a consonant, 는 and 가 after a vowel.

ko.title: Object particle 을/를
ko.explain: 을 (after a consonant) or 를 (after a vowel) marks the direct object of the verb.

ko.title: Place particles 에 and 에서
ko.explain: 에 marks a destination or a place of existence; 에서 marks the place where an action happens.

ko.title: Past tense 았/었어요
ko.explain: Add 았어요 after stems whose last vowel is ㅏ or ㅗ, 었어요 otherwise; 하다 becomes 했어요.

ko.title: Future (으)ㄹ 거예요
ko.explain: Stem + ㄹ 거예요 (vowel stem) or 을 거예요 (consonant stem) expresses a plan or a prediction.
ex: I will meet a friend tomorrow.
I will read a book this evening.

ko.title: Reason 아/어서 and condition (으)면
ko.explain: 아/어서 links a cause to its result (no tense marker before it). (으)면 means if or when.
ex: It rained, so I stayed home.
If you have time, let's go together.

es.title: Ser vs estar
es.explain: Ser is for identity, origin, profession and inherent traits; estar is for location, temporary states and the progressive.

es.title: Present tense of regular verbs
es.explain: -ar: o, as, a, amos, áis, an. -er: o, es, e, emos, éis, en. -ir: o, es, e, imos, ís, en. Latin America uses ustedes instead of vosotros.

es.title: Preterite vs imperfect
es.explain: Preterite for completed, bounded events; imperfect for background, habits and ongoing past states.
ex: Yesterday I went to the market.
Cuando era niño, {jugaba} en la calle.
When I was a child, I used to play in the street.

es.title: Object pronouns
es.explain: Direct: lo, la, los, las. Indirect: le, les (se before lo/la). They go before a conjugated verb or attach to an infinitive.
ex: The book? I already read it.
I gave the keys to María.

es.title: Present subjunctive after wishes and doubt
es.explain: After querer que, esperar que, es posible que, etc., the second verb takes the subjunctive.
ex: I want you to come to my party.
I hope you have a good day.

es.title: Por vs para
es.explain: Para: purpose, destination, deadline, recipient. Por: cause, duration, exchange, movement through.

pt.title: Ser vs estar
pt.explain: Ser for identity, origin and permanent traits; estar for location of movable things, temporary states and the progressive.

pt.title: Contractions of prepositions with articles
pt.explain: em + o/a = no/na; de + o/a = do/da; a + o/a = ao/à; por + o/a = pelo/pela.
ex: I am going to the market.

pt.title: Present progressive with estar + gerund
pt.explain: Brazilian Portuguese uses estar + -ando / -endo / -indo for actions in progress.

pt.title: Pretérito perfeito
pt.explain: Completed past. -ar: ei, ou, amos, aram. -er: i, eu, emos, eram. -ir: i, iu, imos, iram. Ir and ser share fui, foi, fomos, foram.
ex: Yesterday I went to the beach.

pt.title: Near future with ir + infinitive
pt.explain: The everyday future is ir (vou, vai, vamos, vão) + infinitive.
ex: Tomorrow I am going to work.
We are going to travel in July.

pt.title: Present subjunctive
pt.explain: After querer que, esperar que, talvez, é importante que: -ar verbs take -e, -er/-ir verbs take -a.
ex: I hope you like the gift.
I want you to come with me.

zh.title: 是 for identity, 很 with adjectives
zh.explain: 是 links two nouns. Adjectives act as predicates without 是; a neutral statement usually takes 很.

zh.title: Questions with 吗 and 呢
zh.explain: 吗 at the end turns a statement into a yes/no question. 呢 bounces a question back: and you?

zh.title: Measure words
zh.explain: A number or 这/那 needs a measure word before the noun: 个 (general), 本 (books), 件 (clothes, matters), 杯 (cups).
ex: I want to buy a shirt.

zh.title: Location with 在
zh.explain: 在 + place comes before the verb to say where an action happens; on its own it means to be at.

zh.title: Completed action 了 and experience 过
zh.explain: 了 after a verb marks completion. 过 after a verb marks having had the experience at some time.

zh.title: The 把 construction
zh.explain: Subject + 把 + object + verb + result. It stresses what is done to the object.
ex: I left my keys at home.

de.title: Present tense and verb second
de.explain: Regular endings: -e, -st, -t, -en, -t, -en. The conjugated verb is always the second element of a main clause.
ex: Today she is working at home.

de.title: Accusative case
de.explain: The direct object takes the accusative: only masculine changes (der → den, ein → einen).

de.title: Perfekt with haben or sein
de.explain: Spoken past: haben/sein + past participle at the end. Sein with verbs of movement or change of state.

de.title: Dative after certain prepositions
de.explain: aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu always take the dative: dem, der, dem, den (+n).

it.title: Essere and avere
it.explain: Essere: sono, sei, è, siamo, siete, sono. Avere: ho, hai, ha, abbiamo, avete, hanno. Age and hunger use avere.

it.title: Definite articles
it.explain: il / lo / l' / la in the singular; i / gli / le in the plural. Lo and gli before s + consonant, z, gn, ps.

it.title: Passato prossimo
it.explain: avere or essere + past participle. With essere the participle agrees with the subject.

it.title: Articulated prepositions
it.explain: di, a, da, in, su combine with the article: del, al, dal, nel, sul and their feminine and plural forms.
ex: I am going to the restaurant.
The book is on the table.
